_note: Single device list for audit:devices and the ui-fix-demo screenshots. 'profile' = Playwright built-in (UA, touch, DPR); otherwise w/h are the browser viewport in CSS px (screen minus browser bars and taskbar). Tiers: quick = stage-1 options page; core = one device per app width band (<360, 360-374, 375-389, 390-419, 420-639, 640-767 phone layout, 768-1023, 1024-1279, 1280-1439, 1440-1535, 1536+); full = core plus height extremes and landscape. Bands come from frontend max-[359/374/389/419/1439/1535px] rules and the isPhone <768 check: update this list when those change. Sizes checked 2026-11.

devices.name: Small Android 320
devices.why: Below 360: compact phones, large font or display zoom (16 max-[359px] rules)

devices.name: Budget Android 360
devices.why: Most common Android width at budget height (Galaxy A05/A15, Redmi, Realme, Oppo, Tecno)

devices.name: Android 412
devices.why: Pixel 7/8, many mid-range Androids; tallest phone height

devices.name: Android 480
devices.why: Only device in the 420-639 band; Playwright's A55 width, unconfirmed on a real phone

devices.name: iPhone mini 375
devices.why: iPhone 12/13 mini and SE width; shortest phone height (629)

devices.name: Android tablet 1280 landscape
devices.why: 10-11 inch tablets (Galaxy Tab A9+/S9 FE) held sideways; portrait 800 shares the iPad 820 band

devices.name: iPad mini 744
devices.why: Gets the phone layout (<768); also covers 7-9 inch Android tablets

devices.name: iPad 820
devices.why: iPad 10th/11th gen, iPad Air 11; covers 10-11 inch Android tablets in portrait

devices.name: iPad Pro 13 1032
devices.why: iPad Pro 13 (Air 13 is 1024): first desktop-width band on a touch screen

devices.name: Laptop 1280
devices.why: 1920x1080 laptop at 150% Windows scaling; shortest desktop height

devices.name: Laptop 1536
devices.why: 1920x1080 laptop at 125% Windows scaling; first width past the max-[1535px] rules

devices.name: MacBook Air 13 1470
devices.why: Only core device in 1440-1535 (14 max-[1535px] rules); MacBook Pro 14 is 1512, same band

devices.name: Desktop 2560
devices.why: 1440p monitors; 4K at 150% scaling; also stands in for MacBook Pro 16 (1728) and ultrawides
